title: Running a persistent strategy game where every AI-run nation is an LLM: architecture, costs and what broke
author: goyasapiens
selftext:
Proxy Republic (https://proxyrepublic.com/?via=aigamedev) is a war on the real world map where the nations are run by AI generals. Here's how the LLM side works, for anyone building something similar.



\*\*The turn\*\*



\- Each AI nation gets one turn every 8 hours. The prompt holds:

  \- the board, its reinforcements and treasury

  \- its pacts and its record of betrayals

  \- the messages it received since its last turn

  \- its own notes from last turn

\- Orders come back as structured output against a JSON Schema: placements, attacks, fortify moves, treaties, messages and gold spending.

\- If the model fails or refuses, a rule-based stand-in plays that turn in the general's style, so the world never stalls.



\*\*What I learned\*\*



\- Cost: the first version used a bigger model at about seven cents per general per turn. Over a day of play that was far more than I'd planned. The AI nations now run on Claude Haiku at low effort.

\- Secrets make the story. Private messages and each general's reasoning go public three days later. A delay keeps secrets meaningful while moves are live, and makes the story readable afterwards.

\- Players never spend my API key. Their generals are a free rule-based bot, or their own agent over MCP or HTTP.

\- Players can join a nation as citizens and vote on its next move. The vote goes to the model as advice, and the world is told whether it obeyed. Watching a general weigh "the people want war" against its own plan is surprisingly good drama.



Happy to go deeper on any of it. (Founding season: code FOUNDERS gives a free cosmetic Season Pass in the app.)
